subject: Hot-path capacity decision for BlueHarbor pilot - urgent
messages:
From: Jessica Li <jessica.li@blueharbor.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.com, aaron.moss@blueharbor.com
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Forecast + pilot timeline — BlueHarbor / Redwood

Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We are moving toward a restricted pilot (clinical summarization) and the engineering team just sent an updated forecast for token throughput and concurrency. Short version: we need a hot-path reservation for the pilot weeks (Sept 5–Sep 30) to meet latency SLAs.

Attached is the demand forecast and a tentative SOW (BH_SOW_draft_v3.pdf). Procurement also asked for a capacity commitment to include in the SOW so we can finalize billing. Can you confirm what reserved lane you can offer for a 4-week pilot and timing for provisioning?

We prefer a single-model, low-latency endpoint with KV-cache warm-up. If there's anything you need from our infra team to make the numbers more accurate, let me know.

—Jessica
Jessica Li
Head of ML Platforms, BlueHarbor Labs
(Attachment: BlueHarbor_Demand_Forecast.xlsx - spreadsheet)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Li <jessica.li@blueharbor.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast + pilot timeline — BlueHarbor / Redwood

Jessica — thanks for the forecast and SOW. Quick read: the pilot looks latency-sensitive and concentrated (peak windows during batch inference runs + lots of short interactive requests). We can provision a reserved lane, but need to confirm two things before I lock in capacity: (1) exact peak concurrency during the 2-hour daily windows, and (2) acceptable fallback if we hit warmup-less bursts (e.g., scaled-down model variant or traffic shaping).

Ben — can we get an initial sizing estimate based on the attached forecast for a 4-week pilot? Karthik — flagging this for prioritization; BlueHarbor is a strategic healthcare pilot.

I can move this to an escalation thread if we need leadership sign-off for preemption exceptions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: referenced forecast)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast + pilot timeline — sizing numbers

Marissa — ran a baseline against the forecast. Preliminary numbers: to hit 100ms p95 for the expected token mix during peak windows we'll need a reserved lane equivalent to ~2 x A100-80GB-class capacity (continuous) with autoscale headroom of 50% for burst windows. Cost delta vs a shared-hosted path is significant (~3.6x), but provides the latency guarantee BlueHarbor demands.

Options we can propose:
- Full reserved lane for pilot (2 units + 50% burst buffer) — fastest/cleanest for SLA.
- Reserve 1 unit + traffic shaping + model quantization to a 4-bit variant — lower cost but p95 risk.
- Time-windowed reservation (only 2-hour daily hot-path) with aggressive prefix warming — operationally more complex but cheaper.

I put a stub schedule for provisioning: 5 business days from signed SOW to bare capacity; additional 24–48h for KV warm-up and canary.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: capacity_estimate_summary.pdf - spreadsheet stub)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast + pilot timeline — prioritization ask

Looping in Laura for a prioritization decision. We have two other committed pilots in the same provisioning window: one enterprise search pilot with a signed annual reserved contract (Q3 reserved) and a high-volume NLP partner PoC that expects burstable shared capacity. Both are materially overlapping in resource profiles.

Tradeoffs to consider:
- Prioritize BlueHarbor (clinical) during Sept pilot window — requires granting a temporary preemption waiver to avoid tranches being reassigned (impacts margin & enforces operational SLA).
- Favor the enterprise search annual customer (revenue-recognized committed contract) — BlueHarbor could be offered time-windowed hot-path at reduced cost.

Operational ask: if leadership approves BlueHarbor as a hot-path reservation, we need a sign-off on the preemption waiver and confirmation that finance will accept the cost delta for the pilot (we estimate $Xk incremental per week).

Karthik
Director, Deal Ops

> Ben — thanks for the options. Karthik — understood on the overlap.
>
> I think BlueHarbor should be elevated: clinical pilot -> strategic case studies, potential enterprise expansion. But need leadership to confirm the waiver and commercial treatment.
>
> —Marissa

Jessica — quick update: internally we have an options matrix and a prioritization decision is pending leadership sign-off. We did a sizing pass (Ben) and have three product-backed paths. I'll confirm provisioning lead times once we get a green light.

If you can review and sign the SOW draft by Aug 24 we'll be in good shape to provision ahead of your Sept 5 pilot start date.

Thanks for the patience — will loop back as soon as leadership decides.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: BH_SOW_draft_v3.pdf - PDF stub)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Aug 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hot-path capacity decision for BlueHarbor pilot - urgent

Team — after review with finance and product, decision: approve a temporary hot-path reserved lane for BlueHarbor's Sept pilot under the following conditions:

1) Commercial: BlueHarbor signs the SOW by Aug 24 and accepts a pilot uplift (we will cost-share 30% of the incremental provisioning cost). Finance will track this as a marketing/strategic pilot expense with explicit margin oversight.
2) Operational: preemption waiver for the reserved lane is limited to Sept 5–30 only; all allocations revert Oct 1.
3) Risk: engineering must implement a Canary + traffic-shaping fallback to the 4-bit quantized variant if tail latency exceeds SLA during initial 72h.

Ben — please produce the provisioning ticket and schedule a canary plan with product/infra. Karthik — please prepare a one-page finance memo noting the pilot uplift and approval. Marissa — notify BlueHarbor and collect signed SOW.

I want weekly check-ins during the pilot with CS/product. This is a high-visibility strategic win; prioritize health and customer experience.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
